In the ethylene glycol-based recovery process, the PVDF binder is not removed or dissolved. This is supported by the FTIR spectra in Figure 2a, which show that the characteristic peaks of pristine PVDF are still present in the delaminated electrode. Additionally, the XRD patterns in Figure 2b show that the diffraction peaks of NMC532 before and after delamination are consistent, indicating that the crystal structure of the active material was well-maintained and that no impurities were detected after separation.

In the Cyrene-based recovery process, the PVDF binder is removed. This is supported by the FTIR spectra in Figure 3a, which show that the characteristic peaks of pristine PVDF are absent in the reclaimed cathode powder that was filtered at high temperature (e.g., 100 °C). The absence of the typical band at 871 cm^−1 for the reclaimed powder that was filtered at high temperature demonstrated the removal of PVDF binder.
